claims.text: Palestinians in Gaza stated that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's rejection of the US-backed 15-point peace plan has deepened uncertainty over an end to the war.
Hamas stated that it remains committed to the 15-point peace agreement.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected a US-backed 15-point peace plan for Gaza on August 9, 2026.
Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the Israeli military will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is completely disarmed of all heavy and light weaponry.

Donald Trump's Board of Peace proposed a 15-point plan in July requiring Hamas to disarm in exchange for a full Israeli military withdrawal from Gaza and a transition of power to a Palestinian National Committee.
Nickolay Mladenov, high representative for Gaza for the Board of Peace, stated that the 15-point plan is the only way forward to prevent a recurrence of the conflict.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced at a cabinet meeting that Israeli forces will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas is genuinely disarmed.
US President Donald Trump announced in late July 2026 that his Board of Peace had reached an agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.
A senior Hamas official previously stated that the group would only hand over its weapons if Israel withdrew from parts of Gaza first.
Palestinian officials and aid agencies report that Israel controls roughly 70 percent of Gaza.
A Hamas official told the BBC that the group reaffirms its commitment to the 15-point peace plan and is ready to engage seriously in implementing it.
About 1.9 million people, representing 90% of Gaza's population, have been displaced since the war began.
More than 73,000 people have been killed in Gaza during Israel's military campaign, according to the territory's health ministry.
Far-right members of Netanyahu's cabinet urged him to reject the US-led Gaza plan ahead of Israel's October 27, 2026 elections.
Bassem Naim, a member of Hamas's political bureau, urged mediators and the US to pressure Netanyahu to adhere to the agreed roadmap.
Israeli operations in Gaza have killed 1,258 Palestinians since the October ceasefire, according to the Gaza health ministry.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards stated on August 9, 2026, that they will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the US complies with demands including war damage compensation.
US President Donald Trump told Axios that he is "low-keying it" regarding his administration's military approach to Iran.

Iran's Supreme National Security Council laid out conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, including ending the war, lifting the US blockade of Iranian ports, ending sanctions, releasing frozen assets, and receiving compensation.
Yemen's Houthis announced they struck a Saudi oil facility on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast.
Houthi strikes on the Yemeni port city of Mokha killed three civilians and eight military personnel and injured 32 people.
US President Donald Trump signaled that his administration is easing off potential new military strikes against Iran in favor of economic pressure.
A June 2026 memorandum between the US and Iran included a proposal for a $300 billion reconstruction fund for Iran.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards declared that the Strait of Hormuz is a theatre of war and will remain closed until all conditions are accepted.
Donald Trump stated that lower oil prices slightly above $75 a barrel have reduced economic pressure on American consumers.
Negotiations involving Iran, Oman, and the US regarding reopening the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei to discuss military developments, economic challenges, and people's livelihoods as Pezeshkian entered his third year in office.
Israeli media reported that Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei was in an extremely critical health condition.
Mojtaba Khamenei became Iran's supreme leader following the death of his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in February 28 US-Israeli strikes.
Syria and Russia agreed to end Moscow's military use of Hmeimim air base and Tartous port as military outposts on August 9, 2026.
Under the new Syria-Russia agreement, Damascus will take control of Hmeimim air base and part of Tartous port, while remaining facilities will become joint training centers.
The memorandum of understanding between Syria and Russia sets a deadline of no more than three months to complete the transition of the military bases.
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani inspected Hmeimim airbase and Tartus naval base on August 9, 2026.
Omar al-Hasri, head of Syria's Civil Aviation Authority, announced that the agency is taking control of Latakia's international airport adjacent to Hmeimim.
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has been received twice by Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow since taking power.
Earlier in 2026, the Kremlin withdrew its military forces from Qamishli airport in northeastern Syria.
Russia has reduced its military presence in Syria from over 100 military bases down to two coastal locations.
The Syrian government in Damascus has repeatedly demanded that Russia extradite ousted leader Bashar al-Assad, who is living in Moscow.
Ranchi Police deployed security measures for a planned student protest march to the Jharkhand Assembly on August 10, 2026.
Student leader Ravindra Paswan stated the state government agreed to consider cancelling the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination, JPSC Backlog 2023, and JPSC Backlog 2025 exams.
Student leader Kunal stated that student protesters insist on a CBI inquiry into the JSSC-CGL recruitment examination.
Ranchi City SP Paras Rana clarified that security personnel carried paintball guns to identify troublemakers, not pellet guns as rumoured.
Jharkhand Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar accepted the resignations of three JPSC Commission members: Ajita Bhattacharya, Anima Hansda, and Jamal Ahmed.
The student recruitment protest in Jharkhand entered its 16th day, with six demonstrators on an indefinite hunger strike.
Jharkhand Education Minister Sudivya Kumar stated that the government accepted 98% of the student protesters' demands but rejected a CBI probe into the JSSC-CGL exam.
The Jharkhand government proposed a judicial inquiry headed by a retired high court judge and a CID investigation into criminal cases linked to exam irregularities.
The Jharkhand government promised fast-track courts and stated chargesheets against accused persons would be filed within 90 days.
Minister Sudivya Kumar stated the state government lacks authority to cancel the CGL examination because it was conducted under High Court and Supreme Court supervision.
The Jharkhand government proposed establishing an expert panel with representatives from IIT-ISM, IIM Ranchi, and XLRI to recommend examination system reforms.
Demonstrators surrounded former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's vehicle in Halisahar, North 24 Parganas district, throwing shoes, mud, and stones.
Mamata Banerjee stated that her car was attacked with stones, shoes, and mud, accusing the police of protecting BJP lumpens.
West Bengal BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya denied BJP involvement in the attack on Mamata Banerjee's car and condemned the throwing of stones.
Birju Keot, husband of former municipal councillor Jeni Sharma Keot, died in police custody following his arrest by Halisahar police on extortion allegations.
Trinamool Congress MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee accused the BJP of orchestrating an attempt to murder Mamata Banerjee during her visit.
TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee alleged that West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari directed the attack on Mamata Banerjee's car.
Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen stated that thrown stones and half-bricks cracked the glass of Mamata Banerjee's car.
Local agitators in Halisahar raised slogans of "go back" and "thief" at Mamata Banerjee during her visit on Sunday afternoon.
TMC Lok Sabha member Kalyan Banerjee demanded the immediate resignation of West Bengal's Director General of Police following the incident.
A senior Barrackpore city police officer confirmed that a judicial magistrate enquiry was ordered into Birju Keot's death in custody.
